# WindLoadCalc — windloadcalc.com

> WindLoad Solutions has been calculating wind loads since 2002 and online since 2006 — one of the very first wind load calculators on the web. We sell professional ASCE 7-22 wind load calculation software for structural engineers, architects, and building professionals. Florida-licensed in-house Professional Engineer reviews all jurisdictional override data.

## Primary free resource

- [Free Wind Load Calculator + Wind Speed Lookup](https://windloadcalc.com/free-wind-load-calculator.html): The only free online wind load calculator on the public web that returns the legally enforceable wind speed for Florida HVHZ counties. Enter a ZIP code, get the ASCE 7-22 basic wind speed PLUS Florida Building Code R301.2(7) jurisdictional overrides for Miami-Dade (175 mph Cat II), Broward (170 mph Cat II), and Collier (170 mph Cat II) counties. Also computes single-component design pressure per ASCE 7-22 Chapters 26 and 30 with every coefficient cited to its source section. No signup. No usage meter.
- [Try the wind load calculator free before you buy](https://windloadcalc.com/faq.html): Two free ways to evaluate WindLoadCalc — (1) the free online wind load calculator returns an instant single-component ASCE 7-22 design pressure for any U.S. ZIP with no signup, and (2) a 7-day free trial of the full subscription calculators (multi-opening schedules, all six roof shapes, MWFRS, PE-stampable Engineering Reports, real .xlsx exports) with no credit card. Try before you buy.

## Florida jurisdictional wind speeds (FBC R301.2(7))

These values supersede the ASCE 7-22 basic wind speed map for permit submission in their respective counties:

- **Miami-Dade County (HVHZ)**: Risk Category I = 165 mph, II = 175 mph, III = 186 mph, IV = 195 mph
- **Broward County (HVHZ)**: Risk Category I = 156 mph, II = 170 mph, III = 180 mph, IV = 185 mph
- **Collier County**: Risk Category I = 151 mph, II = 170 mph, III = 180 mph, IV = 190 mph

Multi-opening schedules, PE-stampable PDF reports, real .xlsx exports for AutoCAD, project save, 7-day free trial.

## Florida geographic landing pages

- [Florida Wind Load Calculator (statewide hub)](https://windloadcalc.com/florida-wind-load-calculator): The statewide entry point — ASCE 7-22 baseline plus the three FBC-adopted county overrides (Miami-Dade 175, Broward 170, Collier 170). HVHZ overview, FBC 8th Edition transition, county comparison table.
- [Miami-Dade Wind Load Calculator (HVHZ, 175 mph)](https://windloadcalc.com/miami-dade-wind-load-calculator): The HVHZ specialist page — 175 mph Risk Cat II auto-applied countywide, Notice of Acceptance (NOA) + TAS 201/202/203 protocols referenced on every opening, FBC 8th Edition compliant.
- [Broward Wind Load Calculator (HVHZ, 170 mph)](https://windloadcalc.com/broward-wind-load-calculator): Second HVHZ jurisdiction — 170 mph Risk Cat II auto-applied across all 31 Broward municipalities, NOA cross-acceptance from Miami-Dade product control.
- [Collier County Wind Load Calculator (Naples, Marco, 170 mph)](https://windloadcalc.com/collier-county-wind-load-calculator): WindLoadCalc's home market — Naples-founded 2002. 170 mph SW Florida override (non-HVHZ, FL# Product Approval pathway). Lanai/pool-cage volume specialty.
- [Palm Beach Wind Load Calculator (165-170 mph ZIP gradient)](https://windloadcalc.com/palm-beach-wind-load-calculator): The non-HVHZ neighbor — Palm Beach uses the raw ASCE 7-22 map (no county-wide FBC override coded), producing a 165-170 mph coastal-to-inland gradient resolved at ZIP precision across the five Palm Beach submarkets.

## Methodology + sources

- [Free Wind Load Calculator methodology](https://windloadcalc.com/free-wind-load-calculator.html#methodology): ASCE 7-22 Eq. 26.10-1 and Eq. 30.3-1, with every coefficient (Kz, Kzt, Kd, Ke, GCp, GCpi) referenced to its ASCE 7-22 table, section, or figure number.
- Primary references: ASCE/SEI 7-22, Florida Building Code 8th Edition (2023) Residential R301.2(7), International Building Code 2024 §1609.

## Company

WindLoad Solutions (WindLoadCalc, WLC) — founded in Naples, Florida in 2002 doing wind loads for local architects and engineers. Went online in 2006. 11-year firm head start and 7-year online head start over SkyCiv (founded 2013). In-house Florida-licensed Professional Engineer (kept anonymous in customer-facing copy) reviews jurisdictional override values against current Florida Building Code text.
